scope: Read-only evidence review of the existing workspace; no runtime was started.

hardware_context.known_from_user: RTX 3050 Ti Laptop GPU, 4 GB VRAM, 16 GB RAM.
hardware_context.observed_snapshot: Not sampled for this report. Historical run snapshots are per-run and should not be read as current available RAM.

capabilities.name: Local Japanese TTS with Nino adapter and reference conditioning
capabilities.details: Irodori-TTS-v4.1-Small base plus the run-20261031T165530Z-4ebdab62 best-step-450 adapter; BF16 model and codec on CUDA, Japanese text/caption and reference latent conditioning. The adapter is only one component: the base checkpoint, codec, tokenizers/text encoder, reference data, and runtime also need deployment resources.

capabilities.name: Speaker reference and caption control
capabilities.details: The generator accepts Japanese caption and reference latent inputs; it validates text and caption token counts against the runtime limits. This is conditioned synthesis, not a live voice conversation pipeline.

capabilities.name: Long-form story output
capabilities.details: Eight story scenes have generated outputs and a manifest; individual scenes are generated as complete WAVs. This does not establish continuous streaming playback or interruption support.

capabilities.name: Local GPU execution and resource telemetry
evidence: runtime/irodori_lowmem.py: MemoryGuard and CUDA allocation telemetry
capabilities.details: Example scene peak CUDA allocated/reserved was about 2.32/2.71 GB for 06 and 2.92/3.00 GB for 08, with allocator cap about 3.0 GB. Example host process working set reached about 2.24 GB and private bytes about 6.56 GB in 08; the batch codec run recorded roughly 2.70 GB lowest physical headroom. These vary by run and competing applications.

capabilities.name: Generation timing
capabilities.details: Those examples output 28.16 s in 26.53 s synthesis (RTF 0.942) and 16.52 s in 15.22 s synthesis (RTF 0.921), where synthesis includes the CPU watermark. A cold batch load was 18.66 s (model 11.73, tokenizers 2.20, codec 4.52); this load is excluded from per-scene hot RTF. These are completed-file elapsed times, not first-audio latency.

capabilities.name: Watermark path
capabilities.details: Official SilentCipher CPU FP32 watermark is applied after GPU generation/decoding, in approximately 4-second chunks with overlap. Example CPU watermark time was 17.94 s for the 28.16-second scene and 10.08 s for the 16.52-second scene. Story path may restart into a separate CPU watermark process; cold/load and restart gaps are not the same as interactive response latency.

capabilities.name: Training data / fine-tuning
capabilities.details: The identified run is a fine-tuning artifact and the user reports 380 data items with 30 caption labels. Dataset/model iteration is not the main missing desktop-pet engineering work; do not treat the adapter alone as a deployable TTS system.

interactive_readiness.offline_file_generation_is_not_realtime: Existing RTF near 0.92 means the measured full synthesis plus watermark time was near the resulting audio duration in these examples. Load costs, sequential scene processing, scheduling, and UI/playback are outside that RTF; no live response guarantee follows.

first_audio_latency.status: unknown; existing RTF is not first-audio latency
first_audio_latency.evidence: Existing RTF around 0.92-0.94 is measured for complete audio synthesis and excludes cold loading; no first-chunk timestamp exists. CPU SilentCipher watermark adds material post-generation time (about 10.08 s for a 16.52 s scene and 17.94 s for a 28.16 s scene in cited examples).

true_chunk_streaming.evidence: Reviewed wrapper generates and saves complete scene/utterance audio; it does not expose native incremental audio chunks. Wrapping the completed-WAV path in HTTP does not establish true streaming.
true_chunk_streaming.mvp_route: For MVP, split a complete reply into short Japanese sentences, generate the next sentence while playing the previous one, and measure perceived first audio. This is sentence-level pipelining, not a claim that Irodori itself streams audio.

barging_and_cancel.evidence: No request cancellation or playback interruption path in reviewed runtime.
barging_and_cancel.mvp_acceptance: Add stop/cancel and discard stale queued audio. A <=250 ms stop target is aspirational and unmeasured.

resident_api_or_server.evidence: Reviewed entrypoints are offline CLI/batch scripts and process-separated stages. No resident server/stream endpoint is evidenced; placing HTTP around a complete-WAV request would not by itself provide incremental model streaming.

audio_playback_queue.evidence: Listen HTML pages are for reviewing generated recordings; they are not a desktop playback queue/runtime.

voice_input_vad_asr_echo_handling.evidence: No microphone capture, VAD, live ASR, turn-taking, or echo cancellation path evidenced.

agent_memory_character_knowledge.evidence: Story text/captions and speaker labels exist as authored inputs; no interactive agent, persistent memory, or character knowledge system evidenced.

live2d_desktop_shell_character_assets.evidence: No Live2D runtime, desktop overlay/window shell, or integrated character asset set evidenced. Existing listen pages only expose audio review.

known_constraints_and_unknowns.name: Irodori input limits
known_constraints_and_unknowns.detail: Text and caption token limits are checked against runtime.default_text_max_len/default_caption_max_len in the runner. No fixed max-seconds duration limit was identified in the reviewed wrapper; generated duration is observed output, not evidence of an unlimited request size.

known_constraints_and_unknowns.name: Desktop idle resource budget
known_constraints_and_unknowns.detail: Historical run snapshots show high host-memory pressure and GPU peaks close to the configured cap; idle resident model memory and contention alongside a desktop renderer have not been measured. A previously observed 1.49 GB available RAM was a point-in-time condition, not a machine specification.

known_constraints_and_unknowns.name: Sentence pipelining versus native audio streaming
known_constraints_and_unknowns.detail: MVP can pipeline complete short sentences: generate the next while playing the prior one. This is distinct from native per-utterance audio chunk streaming, which is not evidenced in the reviewed Irodori wrapper. A web/API wrapper alone does not change that.

mvp_acceptance_targets_not_yet_measured: Short Japanese sentence pipeline: generate the next sentence while playing the previous sentence; instrument end-of-user-turn to first playable audio. A <=2.0 s first-audio target is aspirational and unmeasured; report cold start separately.
Stop/cancel target <=250 ms after a new user turn; discard stale queued output. Aspirational and unmeasured.
Resident single process serves multiple requests without reloading; report cold-start separately from warm request latency.
Barge-in test: stop current playback and cancel generation within <= 250 ms after a new user turn; no stale queued audio plays afterward.

Measure full application idle and active host RAM plus GPU allocated/reserved while TTS, UI/Live2D, and playback run together; target <= 12 GB host RAM and <= 3.5 GB VRAM on the known machine, with safety headroom.
Complete a 30-minute soak with no unbounded queue growth, leaked GPU memory, or failed subsequent request.
Verify audio queue behavior for pause/resume, ordering, device loss, and interruption; target playback underruns = 0 during a 10-minute scripted session.
If voice input is in MVP, verify microphone -> VAD -> ASR turn detection and speaker playback echo suppression in a room test; otherwise mark voice input outside MVP explicitly.
Run dialogue and animation together for 10 minutes with no UI stalls; target animation >= 30 FPS and speech-synchronized mouth motion on measured audio frames.
Persist and retrieve a small set of user-approved character facts across app restart; prove the dialogue policy does not invent absent memories.

Preserve the current Irodori watermark processing contract in the normal output path and budget its measured CPU latency; any alternate path must be explicitly designed and reviewed, not silently assumed away.
